flagship.headline: Diana Ross and the Supremes play their last Ed Sullivan Show
flagship.summary_line_1: Diana Ross and the Supremes sang Someday We'll Be Together on CBS's The Ed Sullivan Show on December 21, 1969, their final appearance on the program with Ross singing lead.
flagship.summary_line_2: Ross left for a solo career after a farewell concert in Las Vegas on January 14, 1970, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is the show's official upload of that night's performance.

events.headline: Diana Ross and the Supremes play their last Ed Sullivan Show
events.summary_line_1: Diana Ross and the Supremes sang Someday We'll Be Together on CBS's The Ed Sullivan Show on December 21, 1969, their final appearance on the program with Ross singing lead.
events.summary_line_2: Ross left for a solo career after a farewell concert in Las Vegas on January 14, 1970, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is the show's official upload of that night's performance.

events.headline: Marvin Gaye holds No. 1 with I Heard It Through the Grapevine
events.summary_line_1: Marvin Gaye's I Heard It Through the Grapevine was No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 21, 1968, its second week on top.
events.summary_line_2: The Motown single stayed at No. 1 into 1969, and the clip below is Gaye's official lyric video.

events.headline: Glen Campbell's Wichita Lineman tops the album chart
events.summary_line_1: Glen Campbell's Wichita Lineman was the No. 1 album on the Billboard Top LPs chart dated December 21, 1968, replacing Big Brother and the Holding Company's Cheap Thrills.
events.summary_line_2: The Beatles' White Album took over a week later, and the clip below is the Jimmy Webb title song, a country crossover hit.

events.headline: Janis Joplin debuts her new band in Memphis
events.summary_line_1: Janis Joplin debuted her new band at the second annual Stax-Volt Yuletide Thing in Memphis on December 21, 1968, per the Songfacts timeline.
events.summary_line_2: Keyboardist Bill King's first-hand account recalls a rough night at the Mid-South Coliseum on a Stax bill, and the clip below is Try (Just a Little Bit Harder) from the band's 1969 album.

events.headline: The Beatles throw a Magical Mystery Tour fancy-dress party
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles hosted a fancy-dress party at the Royal Lancaster Hotel in London on December 21, 1967, to celebrate finishing their Magical Mystery Tour TV film, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Paul McCartney and Jane Asher came dressed as a Pearly King and Queen, the film aired on BBC1 five days later, and the clip below is its title song.

events.headline: Clarinets join When I'm Sixty-Four as Strawberry Fields Forever grows
events.summary_line_1: At EMI Studios on December 21, 1966, three clarinettists added George Martin's score to the Beatles' When I'm Sixty-Four in a two-hour session, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: That same day John Lennon added a vocal and Paul McCartney piano to the psychedelic Strawberry Fields Forever, and the clip below is the Beatles' official film for that song.

events.headline: The Beatles start rehearsing Another Beatles Christmas Show
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles began three days of rehearsals at the Hammersmith Odeon in London on December 21, 1964, for Another Beatles Christmas Show, which opened on December 24, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: The Yardbirds were on the bill, I Feel Fine was No. 1 on the UK chart dated December 17, and the clip below is that single.

events.headline: The Singing Nun holds No. 1 in America with Dominique
events.summary_line_1: The Singing Nun's Dominique was No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 21, 1963, its third of four weeks on top.
events.summary_line_2: Sung in French by Belgian nun Jeanine Deckers, it was one of the most unlikely No. 1s of the decade, and the clip below is the original recording.

events.headline: The Beatles' Christmas Saturday Club session airs on the BBC
events.summary_line_1: BBC radio's Saturday Club broadcast a Beatles session on December 21, 1963, taped four days earlier at London's Playhouse Theatre, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: The set included I Want to Hold Your Hand and This Boy, and the clip below is This Boy from that very broadcast, issued on On Air: Live at the BBC Volume 2.

events.headline: The Beatles preview their Christmas Show in Bradford
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Gaumont Cinema in Bradford on December 21, 1963, a preview of The Beatles Christmas Show with Cilla Black, Billy J. Kramer with the Dakotas, the Fourmost and Tommy Quickly, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: A second preview followed in Liverpool the next night before the London run began on December 24, and the clip below is I Want to Hold Your Hand, No. 1 on the UK chart dated December 19.

events.headline: The Beatles play night four of their last Star-Club run
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on December 21, 1962, the fourth night of their final residency there, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Back in London on November 26 they had recorded their next single, Please Please Me, and the clip below is that recording.

events.headline: Frankie Vaughan holds No. 1 in Britain with Tower of Strength
events.summary_line_1: Frankie Vaughan's Tower of Strength was No. 1 on the UK chart dated December 21, 1961, per the Official Charts Company.
events.summary_line_2: Danny Williams's Moon River sat at No. 2 behind it, and the clip below is Vaughan's recording of the Burt Bacharach and Bob Hilliard song.

events.headline: The Beatles play a lunchtime show at the Cavern Club
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played a lunchtime session at the Cavern Club in Liverpool on December 21, 1961, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: That June in Hamburg they had cut Ain't She Sweet for producer Bert Kaempfert, with John Lennon singing, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is that recording.

events.headline: Ornette Coleman records Free Jazz with a double quartet
events.summary_line_1: Ornette Coleman led a double quartet through Free Jazz at A&R Studios in New York on December 21, 1960, per the Jazz Discography Project.
events.summary_line_2: Issued by Atlantic in 1961, the 37-minute group improvisation was cut in one take, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is part one of the jazz landmark.
